document_title: The Every-day Life of Abraham Lincoln: A Narrative And Descriptive Biography With Pen-Pictures And Personal; Recollections By Those Who Knew Him
author: Francis F. Browne
claims: Abraham Lincoln was elected President of the United States on November 6, 1860.
The Presidential campaign of 1860 was characterized by "Wide awake" clubs and enthusiasm in the North, and a bitter and threatening tone in the South.
Lincoln had a substantial majority of the electoral vote (180 to 123), but the popular vote was nearly a million (930,170) against him.
Following the election, Lincoln was immediately visited by people from all over the country seeking to satisfy curiosity or solicit favors.
Lincoln began forming his Cabinet on the morning after the election, and it was almost the same as the one he finally appointed.
The issues of the 1860 Presidential election were largely moral questions.
The 1860 Presidential election was attended by novel and extraordinary circumstances.
The Republican convention of 1860 led to Lincoln's presidential nomination.
Lincoln was an obscure youth at the beginning of his professional life but became President at age fifty.
The joint discussions between Lincoln and Douglas in 1858 were among the ablest forensic debates since the republic's foundation.
The operator of the telegraph in Springfield placed his instrument at the disposal of an individual who stayed there until enough returns indicated the election outcome, around 2 AM on Wednesday.
